notes.content: DIVERSITY REQUIREMENT FOR CAL STATE LA GRADUATION.

The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement , not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University. For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements. Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

notes.content: ACCREDITATION The professional nursing curriculum leads to the Bachelor of Science degree with a major in Nursing (BSN). The BSN undergraduate program is approved by the California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN ) and accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE) 655 K Street, NW Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001. P: 202-887-6791 PROGRAM OVERVIEW The Patricia A. Chin School of Nursing (PACSON) offers four options for attaining the BSN degree that include: The Basic Option (Basic Pre-Licensure) The RN to BSN Option (RN to BSN Transfer) The ADN to BSN Option (Associate Degree in Nursing to BSN Transfer) The ABSN Option (BSN Accelerated) ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS All students who wish to be accepted into the BSN program must submit two applications: one to the University (Cal State Apply) and one to the School of Nursing (Nursing CAS). Transfer students must complete these applications simultaneously regardless of option. Freshmen students complete the Cal State Apply application to be admitted as pre-nursing students and then submit the Nursing CAS at the end of their first year in the program. Applicants to the ABSN option submit the Nursing CAS application first and apply later to the University via Cal State Apply once directed to do so. There are eight prerequisite courses to the BSN program: BIOL 2030 BIOL 2040 CHEM 1010 COMM 1100 ENGL 1010 MICR 2010 MICR 2020 and one of the following two courses: EDFN 1092 MATH 1092 Students are expected to complete these prerequisite classes (or their equivalents) prior to submitting the Nursing CAS application (before applying to Cal State LA for transfer students; while a pre-nursing student for freshmen). Applicants to the BSN program are screened competitively based on the following: Test of Essential Academic Skills (TEAS) exam score Cumulative and prerequisite GPA Volunteer or work healthcare experience within the last 2 years (considered) Each option has specific admission requirements, which are detailed below. 1. The Basic Option The Basic Pre-Licensure Option is for students who do not have an RN license. There are two paths for entrance to this option: Cal State LA Freshmen Students: Must have been admitted to the Pre-Nursing program as an entering freshmen. Pre-nursing students must then follow a prescribed course plan (including the prerequisites listed above) and meet specific requirements to continue in the Pre-Nursing program. Pre-nursing students must submit a Nursing CAS application at the end of their first year to be considered for admission to the BSN Program. New Transfer Students: Must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25 Grades of “B” or better in the first attempt in each of the eight prerequisite courses TEAS score at or above the 70 th percentile in all content areas The following major preparation courses are recommended: NTRS 2500 : Human Nutrition PSY 1500 : Introductory Psychology SOC 2010 : Introduction to Sociology Note: Students can only apply once to the BSN Program at Cal State LA and must either be a Cal State LA pre-nursing student or a new transfer applicant. Students admitted to a major other than Nursing will not be able to change their major to Nursing during their tenure at Cal State LA. 2. The RN to BSN Option There are two paths for entrance to this option: Students who possess a California R.N. License and an Associate of Arts or Associate of Science in Nursing from an accredited program or an NLNAC Accredited diploma. Students in the CA Community College (CC) collaboration. This path utilizes a collaborative model for academic progression in nursing that links Cal State LA with designated CA Community College (CC to facilitate seamless progression to Cal State LA. Students who are interested in applying for this option using this pathway should meet with their CC academic advisor. Students in the Collaborative Model must submit proof of an R.N. license by the second semester following graduation from their ADN Program. Students using either path must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 Grades of “B” or better in the first attempt in each of the eight prerequisite courses TEAS score at or above the 70 th percentile in all content areas Proof of RN License attached to the Nursing CAS application The following major preparation courses are recommended: NTRS 2500 : Human Nutrition PSY 1500 : Introductory Psychology SOC 2010 : Introduction to Sociology 3. The ADN to BSN Option This option is for students who possess an Associate of Arts or Associate of Science degree in Nursing from an accredited program. The courses are offered through special sessions via the College of Professional and Global Education . Students applying to this option must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25 Grades of “B” or better in the first attempt in each of the eight prerequisite courses TEAS score at or above the 40th percentile in all content areas The following major preparation courses are recommended: NTRS 2500 : Human Nutrition PSY 1500 : Introductory Psychology SOC 2010 : Introduction to Sociology 4. The ABSN Option The Accelerated Bachelor of Science in Nursing (ABSN) option is for students who already possess a baccalaureate degree in another field, but do not possess an RN license and are interested in a full-time, intensive accelerated program to earn a BSN degree as second baccalaureate. The courses are offered through special sessions via College of Professional and Global Education . Students applying to this option must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered: Completion of bachelor’s (or higher) degree in a field other than nursing from an accredited institution Minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 semester units Completion of prerequisite science courses with grades of B or better Completion of all other prerequisite courses with grades of C or better TEAS score at or above the 70th percentile (National Percentile rank) in all content areas Top ranking applicants will be invited for an interview. REQUIREMENTS FOR THE DEGREE The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Nursing is 120 units, of which 88-105 units are in the major. Program General Information Students in the nursing program have specific requirements necessary for nursing courses and clinical placements. These requirements can be found in the Undergraduate Student Handbook under Specific Requirements for Nursing Courses on the PACSON website ( calstatela.edu/hhs/nursing ). NCLEX Credits (The Chancellor’s Executive Order [EO] 1084, Section 5) As the California Board of Registered Nursing requires 36 units of the art and science of nursing in pre-licensure programs in preparation for the standardized external National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX), in accordance with the stipulations of this policy, a CSU campus may award up to 30 academic credits using the NCLEX examination to demonstrate prior learning of the pre-licensure art and science of nursing required by the Board of Registered Nursing (Title 5 section 40408). Some courses are open to non-majors who may find one or more courses helpful in achieving their own professional or personal goals.
notes.contentHtml:
ACCREDITATION

The professional nursing curriculum leads to the Bachelor of Science degree with a major in Nursing (BSN). The BSN undergraduate program is approved by the California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN) and accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE) 655 K Street, NW Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001. P: 202-887-6791

PROGRAM OVERVIEW

The Patricia A. Chin School of Nursing (PACSON) offers four options for attaining the BSN degree that include:

  1. The Basic Option (Basic Pre-Licensure)
  2. The RN to BSN Option (RN to BSN Transfer)
  3. The ADN to BSN Option (Associate Degree in Nursing to BSN Transfer)
  4. The ABSN Option (BSN Accelerated)

ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS

All students who wish to be accepted into the BSN program must submit two applications: one to the University (Cal State Apply) and one to the School of Nursing (Nursing CAS).  Transfer students must complete these applications simultaneously regardless of option.  Freshmen students complete the Cal State Apply application to be admitted as pre-nursing students and then submit the Nursing CAS at the end of their first year in the program.  Applicants to the ABSN option submit the Nursing CAS application first and apply later to the University via Cal State Apply once directed to do so.

There are eight prerequisite courses to the BSN program:

  • BIOL 2030 
  • BIOL 2040 
  • CHEM 1010 
  • COMM 1100 
  • ENGL 1010 
  • MICR 2010 
  • MICR 2020 
  • and one of the following two courses:
  • EDFN 1092 
  • MATH 1092 

Students are expected to complete these prerequisite classes (or their equivalents) prior to submitting the Nursing CAS application (before applying to Cal State LA for transfer students; while a pre-nursing student for freshmen).

Applicants to the BSN program are screened competitively based on the following:

  • Test of Essential Academic Skills (TEAS) exam score
  • Cumulative and prerequisite GPA
  • Volunteer or work healthcare experience within the last 2 years (considered)

Each option has specific admission requirements, which are detailed below.

1. The Basic Option

The Basic Pre-Licensure Option is for students who do not have an RN license. There are two paths for entrance to this option:

  • Cal State LA Freshmen Students:  Must have been admitted to the Pre-Nursing program as an entering freshmen. Pre-nursing students must then follow a prescribed course plan (including the prerequisites listed above) and meet specific requirements to continue in the Pre-Nursing program.  Pre-nursing students must submit a Nursing CAS application at the end of their first year to be considered for admission to the BSN Program.
  • New Transfer Students:  Must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered:
  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25
  • Grades of “B” or better in the first attempt in each of the eight prerequisite courses
  • TEAS score at or above the 70th percentile in all content areas

The following major preparation courses are recommended:

    • NTRS 2500: Human Nutrition
    • PSY 1500: Introductory Psychology
    • SOC 2010: Introduction to Sociology

Note: Students can only apply once to the BSN Program at Cal State LA and must either be a Cal State LA pre-nursing student or a new transfer applicant.  Students admitted to a major other than Nursing will not be able to change their major to Nursing during their tenure at Cal State LA.

2. The RN to BSN Option

There are two paths for entrance to this option:

  • Students who possess a California R.N. License and an Associate of Arts or Associate of Science in Nursing from an accredited program or an NLNAC Accredited diploma.
  • Students in the CA Community College (CC) collaboration.  This path utilizes a collaborative model for academic progression in nursing that links Cal State LA with designated CA Community College (CC to facilitate seamless progression to Cal State LA.  Students who are interested in applying for this option using this pathway should meet with their CC academic advisor. Students in the Collaborative Model must submit proof of an R.N. license by the second semester following graduation from their ADN Program.

Students using either path must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered:

  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0
  • Grades of “B” or better in the first attempt in each of the eight prerequisite courses
  • TEAS score at or above the 70th percentile in all content areas
  • Proof of RN License attached to the Nursing CAS application

The following major preparation courses are recommended:

    • NTRS 2500: Human Nutrition
    • PSY 1500: Introductory Psychology
    • SOC 2010: Introduction to Sociology

3. The ADN to BSN Option

This option is for students who possess an Associate of Arts or Associate of Science degree in Nursing from an accredited program.  The courses are offered through special sessions via the College of Professional and Global Education.

Students applying to this option must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered:

  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25
  • Grades of “B” or better in the first attempt in each of the eight prerequisite courses
  • TEAS score at or above the 40th percentile in all content areas

The following major preparation courses are recommended:

    • NTRS 2500: Human Nutrition
    • PSY 1500: Introductory Psychology
    • SOC 2010: Introduction to Sociology

4. The ABSN Option

The Accelerated Bachelor of Science in Nursing (ABSN) option is for students who already possess a baccalaureate degree in another field, but do not possess an RN license and are interested in a full-time, intensive accelerated program to earn a BSN degree as second baccalaureate. The courses are offered through special sessions via College of Professional and Global Education.

Students applying to this option must meet the following minimum application requirements to be considered:

  • Completion of bachelor’s (or higher) degree in a field other than nursing from an accredited institution
  • Minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 semester units
  • Completion of prerequisite science courses with grades of B or better
  • Completion of all other prerequisite courses with grades of C or better
  • TEAS score at or above the 70th percentile (National Percentile rank) in all content areas

Top ranking applicants will be invited for an interview.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE DEGREE

The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Nursing is 120 units, of which 88-105 units are in the major.

Program General Information

  1. Students in the nursing program have specific requirements necessary for nursing courses and clinical placements. These requirements can be found in the Undergraduate Student Handbook under Specific Requirements for Nursing Courses on the PACSON website (calstatela.edu/hhs/nursing).
  2. NCLEX Credits

(The Chancellor’s Executive Order [EO] 1084, Section 5)

As the California Board of Registered Nursing requires 36 units of the art and science of nursing in pre-licensure programs in preparation for the standardized external National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX), in accordance with the stipulations of this policy, a CSU campus may award up to 30 academic credits using the NCLEX examination to demonstrate prior learning of the pre-licensure art and science of nursing required by the Board of Registered Nursing (Title 5 section 40408).

  1. Some courses are open to non-majors who may find one or more courses helpful in achieving their own professional or personal goals.
